components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one dominant action per screen: filled Meter Yellow with dark text.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #FFD600; color: #374151; border: none; border-radius: 12px; padding: 14px 24px; font-family: Tajawal, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; transition: filter 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.05); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F5F6F7; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { filter: brightness(0.95); }

components.name: Outlined Button
components.description: Secondary action in Amber with a 1.5dp outline.
components.css: .ds-btn-outlined { background: transparent; color: #F59E0B; border: 1.5px solid #F59E0B; border-radius: 12px; padding: 14px 24px; font-family: Tajawal, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-outlined:hover { background: #3D2A14; } .ds-btn-outlined:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F5F6F7; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Cancel and delete actions in Stop Red.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { background: #DC2626; color: #FFFFFF; border: none; border-radius: 12px; padding: 14px 24px; font-family: Tajawal, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { filter: brightness(1.08); } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F5F6F7; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Dash Surface fill with a steel border that turns Meter Yellow on focus.
components.css: .ds-input { background: #1E1F22; color: #F5F6F7; border: 1px solid #34363B; border-radius: 12px; padding: 14px 16px; font-family: Tajawal, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #999DA6; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border: 1.5px solid #FFD600; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat Dash Surface container separated from the page by a 1dp border, with no shadow.
components.html:
Total income this month

components.css: .ds-card { background: #1E1F22; border: 1px solid #34363B; border-radius: 16px; padding: 16px; font-family: Tajawal, sans-serif; } .ds-card-title { color: #B4B8C0; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; } .ds-card-figure { color: #F5F6F7; font-size: 26px; font-weight: 800; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; margin-top: 4px; }

⏱
Waiting at pickup

components.description: Pill showing the chosen role, with an Amber change action.

components.description: Shared 60dp bar; Amber for the active destination, gray for the rest.
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; height: 60px; background: #1E1F22; border-top: 1px solid #26282C; box-shadow: 0 -3px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.10); font-family: Tajawal, sans-serif; } .ds-nav-item { flex: 1; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; color: #9CA3AF; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 400; cursor: pointer; } .ds-nav-active { color: #F59E0B; font-weight: 600; } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F5F6F7; }

narrative.overview:
Picture the inside of a cab at night: dark, quiet, and lit by one warm source, the meter or the roof sign. Near-black surfaces recede into a cabin, and a single yellow does the work of light. It tells a customer this is their next action and a driver this is the number that matters. Everything else is steel-gray text and tonal layers so that the yellow stays rare and means something.

The voice is calm, confident and utilitarian: built for scanning, with big filled tactile controls, clear 1dp borders around cards, tabular figures for money and clocks, and status shown by color plus icon plus text.
keyCharacteristics: One dark theme; yellow #FFD600 is the single dominant signal, amber #F59E0B its secondary.
Depth by tonal layering and hairline borders, not shadows.
Filled, generously rounded (12–16dp) controls with large touch areas.
Tajawal throughout, with heavy weights (700–800) for figures and headings.
Semantic color always paired with an icon or label.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: Yellow is the only light in the cabin. If a screen has more than a few yellow things, one of them has stopped meaning 'act here' or 'this is the number'.

rules.name: The Wash Rule
rules.body: Colored content sits on its tinted wash (yellow on yellow-wash, red on red-wash), never directly on black.

rules.name: The Paired Signal Rule
rules.body: Status is never color alone. Pair green, red and amber with an icon and a word.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Anything that counts or sums (timers, fares, fees, earnings) uses tabular figures and the heaviest weight in its row.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: A surface in a list or a stack gets a border, not a shadow. Shadow is a response to being above something else.

dos: Do keep Meter Yellow rare: one primary action per screen, plus the few places that mean "this is the number".
Do put dark text (On-Yellow Slate #374151) on yellow, always.
Do build from the existing tokens (AppColors, AppConstants radii and padding, and the theme's text roles) and reuse the widgets in core/widgets/ before creating new ones.
Do pair every status color with an icon and a label.
Do use tabular figures and heavy weight for money and clocks.
Do use direction-aware spacing and alignment so every screen mirrors correctly in Arabic.
Do keep touch targets at 48dp or more, with at least 8dp between them.
Do show loading, success and error states on every async surface.
donts: Don't introduce a light theme or invert colors; the system is dark-only.
Don't hardcode hex colors or Colors.white/black/red in feature code. Use AppColors.
Don't add drop shadows to cards in lists; use the border.
Don't use gradients on routine surfaces; the yellow-to-amber gradient is reserved for hero summaries and brand accents.
Don't hand-pick font sizes per widget; map text to the theme's roles.
Don't convey state by color alone.
Don't use orange-red or another warm color that could be read as the error color.
Don't stack primary buttons; one primary action per view.
